test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which authority is the appellate body under the RTI Act?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Information Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Central Information Commission (CIC):** The **Central Information Commission** is the designated appellate authority under the **Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005**. It addresses grievances and resolves disputes related to RTI requests.
 
• The CIC is responsible for ensuring transparency and accountability in the functioning of public authorities by adjudicating appeals and complaints filed under the RTI Act.
 
• The commission functions as an independent body and has the authority to summon public officials, review documents, and order disclosure of information if required. *Hence, the correct answer is Central Information Commission.*
 
• **Structure of the CIC:** The commission consists of the **Chief Information Commissioner** and up to ten **Information Commissioners**, appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners have a tenure of **five years** or until they reach the age of **65 years**, whichever is earlier.
 
• **Role in RTI:** The CIC acts as a final appellate authority to hear appeals against decisions made by the Public Information Officer (PIO) or the First Appellate Authority in cases where applicants are dissatisfied with the responses received.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right to Information Act, 2005:**

 
 
• The **RTI Act** was enacted to promote transparency and accountability in the functioning of public authorities.
 
• It gives citizens the right to access information held by public authorities, subject to certain exemptions and conditions.
 
• The act applies to all levels of government—**Central, State, and local bodies**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Central Information Commission:**
 
 
• The CIC adjudicates on appeals and complaints related to RTI applications, ensuring compliance with the RTI Act.
 
• It has the power to direct public authorities to take necessary actions, such as providing information or justifying its denial.
 
• The CIC can impose penalties on public officials for non-compliance or delay in providing information.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Commissioners:**
 
 
• The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners are appointed by the President of India based on recommendations by a committee comprising the Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and a Union Cabinet Minister.
 
• This ensures that the commission operates independently and impartially.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Exemptions under RTI Act:**

 
 
• Certain sensitive information is exempted from disclosure under the RTI Act, including matters related to **national security, sovereignty, and integrity of India.**
 
• Information prohibited by **courts of law** or relating to commercial confidence, trade secrets, or intellectual property is also exempted.
 
 
 
• **Other Authorities Mentioned in the Options:**
 
 
• **Chief Vigilance Commission:** This authority deals primarily with vigilance and corruption cases in government offices and does not have a role in RTI appeals.
 
• **National Human Rights Commission:** The NHRC addresses issues related to human rights violations and does not serve as the appellate authority under the RTI Act.
 
• **Lokpal:** Lokpal is an anti-corruption ombudsman that investigates complaints of corruption against public officials. It is not involved in RTI appeals.
